name: Jaina permutations and combinations
summary: Jaina texts treated counting of permutations and combinations alongside multi-level infinities.

name: Diophantus
summary: Arithmetica introduced symbols for unknowns and sought rational solutions to polynomial equations.

name: Discovery of incommensurable magnitudes
summary: The failure of the hypotenuse of a right isosceles triangle to be a ratio of integers broke the identification of magnitude with number and forced a new foundation for geometry.

name: Chinese remainder theorem
summary: A single-remainder puzzle grew into a general method for systems of congruences, including non-coprime moduli, motivated by calendar calculation.

name: Indian sine
summary: Siddhantic astronomy replaced chords by half-chords, giving the sine; Aryabhata tabulated it.

name: Indian zero and place value
summary: Brahmi digits developed into a positional decimal system whose schools around 500-650 CE worked out place value and zero.

name: Interpolation and finite differences from Chinese astronomy
summary: Second- and third-order difference methods in astronomy were later used by Zhu Shijie to sum sequences.

name: Indian indeterminate/Pell equations
summary: Integer solutions of equations of the form N x^2 + 1 = y^2 were found by composition and cyclic methods, including the case 61 with a very large minimal solution.

name: Algebra as a discipline (al-Khwarizmi)
summary: Problem-solving with unknowns is organised around a small set of normal-form equations with systematic geometric justification, giving algebra its own objects and rules.

name: Transmission of Hindu-Arabic numerals to the Islamic world
summary: A treatise on Indian decimal calculation, later translated into Latin, spread the positional system and gave 'algorithm' its name.
